answer: Memory-hard proof of work. For a falcon census, summit weather report, or onyx assay, require a fresh puzzle bound to the account and epoch. The verifier checks the target and rejects reused proofs. Allocate rewards in proportion to verified work, with no bonus per identity. Splitting a fixed computing budget among N accounts then adds no expected reward; more accepted proofs require more computation and energy. This assumes puzzles cannot be precomputed or shared across accounts; cheaper hardware or power still gives an advantage.
